newsitem.title: USA: California Utilities in pact on cost of capital.
newsitem.headline: California Utilities in pact on cost of capital.

text.p: Pacific Gas and Electric Co said it and other California utilities have reached an agreement with the state's Division of Ratepayer Advocates and other intervenors to make a joint recommendation in the 1997 Cost of Capital proceeding before state regulators.
The company's "Inside PG&E" newsletter for the financial community said the joint recommendation reached August 27 specifies a return on common equity of 11.6 percent for Pacific Gas," it said.
The utility noted that would represent no change from its current authorized ROE.
The company had requested 11.85 percent and the division had recommended 11.25 percent.
If adopted by the California Public Utilities Commission, the recomendation would result in a 9.45 percent return on utility rate base, the company said.
PG&E's electric and natural gas revenues would decrease about $5 million and $2 million a year, respectively, due to changes in proportion of long-term debt and preferred stock.
The company said the commission is due to make a decision on the recomendation in November. Other utilities operating in the state include Edison International and Enova Corp.
